item.title: Skechers CFO John Vandemore joins Levi Strauss as CFO effective November 1
item.description:
John Vandemore, who spent nearly nine years as Skechers’ chief financial officer, will succeed Harmit Singh as Levi Strauss & Co.’s CFO starting November 1. The move comes as Levi’s aims to grow to $10 billion in annual revenue, a target also matched by Skechers’ recent sales figure.
Before joining Skechers, Vandemore held finance and operations leadership roles at Mattel, The Walt Disney Company, International Game Technology, and various consulting firms. Harmit Singh, who is retiring after many years at Levi’s, will remain as an adviser until November 30. Skechers’ revenue grew from $4 billion in 2017 to $10 billion in the most recent fiscal year, while Levi’s reported that direct‑to‑consumer sales accounted for just over half of its revenue in the latest quarter, rising 11% year‑over‑year.
“Mr. Vandemore previously served as the CFO of Skechers for 9 years, helping the company become one of the world’s largest footwear brands with over $9 billion in revenue,” Tom Nikic, Needham analyst said.
“John’s deep financial, operational and consumer experience, combined with his proven ability to help global brands scale and grow profitably, makes him the ideal partner to help us realize our ambition of becoming a $10 billion company,” Michelle Gass, Levi’s CEO said.
Harmit Singh announced his retirement as Levi Strauss & Co. CFO earlier this year and will stay on as an adviser until November 30. Under Vandemore’s tenure, Skechers’ revenue increased from $4 billion in 2017 to $10 billion in the most recent year, strengthening the shoe maker’s financial profile.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/skechers-cfo-jumps-levis/831872)

item.title: KnitWell Group names Angelica Munson chief digital and customer data officer
item.description:
KnitWell Group appointed Angelica Munson as its chief digital and customer data officer on September 22, according to a press release. In the newly created role, Munson will oversee customer data, insights, AI-assisted marketing tools, personalization and digital marketing for the company’s enterprise strategy.
Munson previously served as global chief digital officer at Shiseido Group, where she led the launch of the Beauty Tech Lab that offered AI-based skin diagnostics.
“Angelica is a highly respected digital and transformation leader whose experience sits at the intersection of customer insight, technology, marketing, and commerce,” Lizanne Kindler said.
KnitWell Group was created three years ago when Ann Taylor, Loft and Talbots were combined under a single holding company. Sycamore Partners acquired the Ascena brands Ann Taylor, Loft, Lane Bryant and Lou & Grey in the bankruptcy process and later purchased Chico’s FAS for $1 billion in 2024, adding White House Black Market and Soma to the group.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/knitwell-chief-digital-customer-data-officer-ann-taylor-chicos/831807)

item.title: Consumer confidence drops to 12‑year low of 81.8 as inflation worries rise
item.description:
The Conference Board reported that the U.S. consumer confidence index fell 6.7 points this month to 81.8, marking a 12‑year low. Median inflation expectations for the next year rose 0.3 points to 5.1%, while the share of households expecting higher interest rates in the next 12 months jumped 5.2 points to 68.4%.
The drop reflects higher fuel prices, increased borrowing costs and employer hiring anxiety, according to the Conference Board. New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said there is no urgent need for another rate increase, projecting inflation to end 2026 at 3.5% and unemployment to ease from 4.1% to 4% over the coming year. Traders lowered the odds of a rate hike at the Oct. 28 Fed meeting to 47% from 71% on Monday, while a NABE survey showed 49% of economists view policy as too stimulative, up 38 points since February.
“Consumers are more disgruntled and squeezed in this economy than they felt during the 2020 pandemic,” Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union said.
The Conference Board noted that its survey aligned with the University of Michigan’s Friday release. Michigan’s survey showed consumer sentiment at a four‑month low and personal‑finance views down about 10%.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/consumer-confidence-sags-12-year-low-eroded-inflation-job-anxiety-fed-federal-reserve/831783)

item.title: SH 130 toll road sees 130% truck traffic rise as fleets seek safer, faster route
item.description:
Heavy truck traffic on the southern 41‑mile stretch of SH 130 has risen nearly 130% since 2019, according to the road’s operator. Drivers on SH 130 are 80% less likely to experience a crash than those on I‑35, making it a safer alternative for fleets.
quotes
“The cost of time spent sitting in I-35 congestion — including increased fuel consumption, lost revenue and late fees for freight carriers — can be two to three times the cost of the SH 130 toll,” Ryan Sethness, Head of Freight Business Development, SH 130 Concession Company said.
context
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/sh-130-a-smarter-safer-route-through-central-texas)

item.title: H&M Kids launches Strawberry Thief childrenswear line with Morris & Co on 8 Oct
item.description:
H&M Kids has teamed up with Morris & Co to release a childrenswear collection featuring Strawberry Thief print, set to launch on 8 October in selected online markets. The line includes smocked dresses, matching sets and scalloped‑collar blouses in a palette of taupe, ivory, chestnut, dusky pink and deep teal, using brushed knit, corduroy and wool‑mix fabrics.
According to the brand, the collection captures the feeling of an English autumn, blending nostalgic heritage with modern wearability. Pieces are designed for everyday kidswear, aiming to feel rooted in craft but ready for real life.
“Our collaboration with Morris & Co. takes the storytelling of Strawberry Thief and brings it into everyday kidswear – pieces that feel rooted in craft but ready for real life. Together, we’ve created a collection that is about heritage made playful,” Sofia Löfstedt, head of kidswear design at H&M said.
“Strawberry Thief is all about celebrating the small, wild details in daily life, which felt like the perfect starting point for a children’s collection. The story of thrushes visiting the kitchen garden of Morris’ countryside home is an idyllic fairy tale in itself, and working with H&M brings these designs to a new generation, in pieces made to be worn, loved and lived in,” Jessica Clayworth, at Morris & Co said.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/hm-and-morris-co-collection)

item.title: Retailers pay 72p tax per £1 profit as sector’s tax bill hits £62bn
item.description:
Retailers and hospitality businesses paid 72p and 82p in tax for every £1 of pre‑tax profit respectively, with the two sectors together contributing £62bn in business taxes during 2025/26. Retail employment fell by 122,000 jobs and hospitality by 93,000 over the past two years.
The £62bn tax bill includes VAT, business rates, employer National Insurance contributions and other taxes. Retail and hospitality together account for almost a third of all revenue raised from the property tax, while one in seven high‑street properties nationwide is currently vacant. The BRC has warned that the rising tax burden is already causing job losses and shuttered shops, limiting the sector’s ability to invest and keep prices down. Ahead of the Budget, the BRC and UKHospitality are calling on Chancellor John Healey to ease the tax burden on high‑street firms, for example by taking retail and hospitality properties out of the government’s high‑value business rates multiplier.
“job losses,” Helen Dickinson, BRC chief executive said.
“more than 750,000 retail, hospitality and leisure properties already benefit from lower business rates multipliers,” Government spokesperson said.
The BRC previously said retail taxes have risen 20 percent over the past two years, leaving the sector paying £1.8bn more in business rates than it did two years ago. Ahead of the upcoming Budget, the BRC and UKHospitality are urging Chancellor John Healey to reduce the high‑street cost burden, including removing retail and hospitality properties from the government’s high‑value business rates multiplier.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/retailers-pay-72p-in-tax-for-every-1-of-profit)

item.title: H&M Group partners with Bleckmann to support UK expansion
item.description:
H&M Group has confirmed a new partnership with fashion logistics specialist Bleckmann to act as its third‑party logistics provider in the UK. The deal will see Bleckmann install an advanced AutoStore system at its Crick, Northamptonshire warehouse to boost flexibility, capacity and fulfilment efficiency.
The Crick site lies within Bleckmann’s Midlands ‘Golden Triangle’ network, where the logistics provider is making further investment to increase UK capacity. H&M will use the facility to manage logistics for a number of its brands, though the exact portfolio names were not disclosed. Bleckmann already handles logistics for fashion names such as Superdry, Gymshark and Blakely, and added sustainable footwear brand Nuoceans as a client in June. Earlier this year, dancewear brand Capezio also named Bleckmann its third‑party logistics provider for warehousing and distribution.
“essential to meeting the growing demand from existing and new clients,” Reinardt van Oel, chief operations officer for Belgium and the UK said.
“proud to now count H&M Group among our clients,” Reinardt van Oel, chief operations officer for Belgium and the UK said.
The site sits within Bleckmann’s Midlands ‘Golden Triangle’ network, with the group making further investment in its UK operations to boost capacity. Bleckmann already works with brands including Superdry, Gymshark and Blakely, while Belgian-British sustainable footwear brand Nuoceans appointed the business as its logistics partner in June.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/hm-group-taps-bleckmann-to-support-uk-expansion)

item.title: Kiehl’s opens 1,300‑sq‑ft experiential flagship on London’s Carnaby Street
item.description:
Kiehl’s has opened a 1,300‑sq‑ft experiential flagship on London’s Carnaby Street. The two‑storey unit marks Kiehl’s second standalone store in the West End and the first content studio the brand has launched in Europe.
The flagship features skin‑analysis technology, a photo booth and custom screen‑printing stations on the ground floor. An interactive Brew Bar matches skincare ingredients to customers’ moods and skin concerns, while Derma Readers provide personalised skin analysis. The entire upper floor is devoted to a content studio for creators, filming and community events, which Kiehl’s said is a first for the brand in Europe. Kiehl’s operates 18 boutiques across the UK, where Britain ranks among its three largest markets, and its Creamy Eye Treatment with Avocado is the UK’s best‑selling prestige eye cream according to L’Oréal.
“want to spend time in,” Niki Lo, UK general manager said.
“meaningful investment in the future of physical retail,” Melanie Vidal, global brand president said.
Kiehl’s is approaching its 175th anniversary and has been investing in standalone stores to boost customer acquisition, loyalty and brand engagement. It currently operates 18 boutiques in the UK, where Britain is one of the brand’s three largest markets.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/kiehls-opens-experiential-european-flagship-on-carnaby-street)

item.title: OpenAI’s ChatGPT ad measurement gaps keep marketer budgets at test level
item.description:
Seven months after OpenAI began selling ads in ChatGPT, marketers still struggle to measure campaign performance, leaving budgets at test levels. Agencies report that ChatGPT shows around 100 clicks while their own logs record only 20, and conversions appear 24 to 36 hours later than on Google.
Many advertisers have not enabled conversion tracking because signing OpenAI’s tracking terms raises legal concerns about liability and data use. OpenAI’s conversions API could improve attribution, but enterprise clients are slow to adopt it and smaller firms often lack the staff to set it up correctly. As a result, most campaigns are still optimized toward clicks or impressions rather than cost‑per‑acquisition or return on ad spend.
“The transition now that we are able to optimize to CPA, rather than focusing on CPC and leading metrics, has been pivotal,” Jellyfish’s Victor Batista, senior paid media director said.
“I think with time, as they gain confidence in their measurement suite, we will see further evolution, and platform confidence will improve as more data is analyzed across partners,” Jellyfish’s Victor Batista, senior paid media director said.
OpenAI introduced ads in ChatGPT seven months ago, but its measurement tools have remained basic, prompting marketer frustration.
Source: Digiday (https://digiday.com/marketing/openais-measurement-gaps-are-keeping-chatgpt-ads-budgets-at-test-level)

item.title: Creators boost AI adoption to 87% as YouTube adds agentic tools
item.description:
Over the past year, 87% of creators have increased their use of AI in content creation, and 86% plan to raise it further in the next 12 months. This growth comes after an early‑year rejection of AI‑generated content and coincides with YouTube’s addition of agentic features such as video A/B testing and conversational editing.
YouTube’s new Ask Studio tool, powered by Gemini, lets creators upload multiple video versions and predicts which version will keep viewers watching the longest. CapCut and Adobe Firefly provide AI‑driven editing suites that creators use for tasks ranging from brainstorming to file organization, while brands worry that AI‑flagged posts could trigger platform penalties dubbed “AI jail”. Creators such as Gigi Robinson employ AI for analytics and task management, yet concerns persist that heavy reliance on generative AI could erode authenticity and lead to homogeneous content.
“I think it’s a lot harder to be super binary because it’s just crept into our everyday so much,” Lucy Kruszynski said.
“I don’t think brands care outside of like, ‘is this content going to be flagged as AI? And if it is, will I get into AI jail or algorithm jail?’ That’s the tricky part,” Keith Bendes said.
Earlier in the year, after the release of OpenAI’s Sora 2, the creator economy loudly denounced generative AI content in favor of authenticity. YouTube removed AI slop accounts, Instagram CEO Adam Mosseri issued a memo urging higher ranking for originality, and brands sought the messiness and creativity of real creators.
Source: Digiday (https://digiday.com/media/the-creator-economys-stance-on-ai-is-shifting-again)

item.title: Amazon says 20% of brand value appears after ad attribution window closes.
item.description:
Amazon says about 20% of a brand’s sales value appears after the standard 7‑ to 30‑day ad attribution window ends, based on a study of over two million June campaigns. The finding underpins Amazon’s push to count ad impact over a full year, using a long‑term sales metric first tested in a closed beta since October 2024.
The metric tracks new‑to‑brand shoppers, notes their first ad‑driven actions like a brand search or cart add, and applies the brand’s past 12‑month return from similar shoppers to forecast annual sales. Amazon has also rolled out full‑funnel campaigns, announced last November, that shift budgets across Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, display and streaming to encourage longer‑term purchases. Soon marketers will be able to compare projected long‑term sales with actual results in Amazon’s clean room, while the platform now provides agencies with 90 days of historical sales data—short of the roughly 18 months many models require.
“What we actually find is that roughly 20% of the sales value for a brand shows up over time and isn’t captured in that immediate attribution window because that’s just a cutoff date for measurement,” Lily Tong, a director of measurement at Amazon Ads said.
Amazon believes its advertising drives more sales than the short attribution windows currently show. Demonstrating that longer‑term impact is becoming a basic requirement, and Amazon faces the same pressure as Google to prove it. While improved upper‑funnel tools and AI shopping shift spend away from search, platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and creators often claim credit for purchases that ultimately occur on Amazon.
Source: Digiday (https://digiday.com/media-buying/amazon-wants-to-own-the-long-game-in-ad-measurement)

item.title: AI agents show 177 toy brands but nearly all picks come from Amazon’s own store
item.description:
Jellyfish’s Share of Model tool found that Alexa for Shopping recommended toys from 177 brands, with nearly all selections coming from Amazon’s own store. By contrast, ChatGPT suggested 24 retailers and Google’s AI Mode suggested 37 for the same toy request.
The Share of Model tool tracked recommendations from Alexa, ChatGPT and Google’s AI Mode across eight categories in the United States, United Kingdom, Australia and Singapore. In July, Copilot’s top 100 e-commerce sites accounted for 34% of its citations, a share more than triple Google’s AI Mode and eight times ChatGPT’s. A Dentsu Creative survey of 1,950 senior marketers in 14 markets found 59% are optimizing content for AI-enabled search while half are investing in agentic commerce. Adobe’s analysis of more than one trillion U.S. retail site visits showed AI-referred shoppers generated 53% higher revenue per visit than other traffic in July.
The article describes AI agents as emerging gatekeepers that choose products for shoppers using algorithms marketers do not fully understand. It notes that marketers have begun tailoring content and investing in agentic commerce to improve visibility in those AI-driven recommendations.
Source: Digiday (https://digiday.com/marketing/in-graphic-detail-where-brands-stand-when-ai-agents-do-the-shopping)

item.title: Seeteria AI uses existing warehouse cameras to cut idle dock time
item.description:
Seeteria’s AI platform flags idle dock doors that sit for as long as 7 minutes, helping warehouses recover lost capacity without new hardware. Small disruptions of 7 to 15 minutes each can compound into hours of missed capacity per shift, according to the founder.
The platform connects to a facility’s existing camera network over Wi‑Fi, analyzes activity in real time, and sends color‑coded alerts — green, yellow, red — to supervisors’ mobile or tablet apps showing the status of each dock door and zone. Floor supervisors receive live push alerts, warehouse managers get a post‑shift summary of bottlenecks, and executives view a financial‑impact report tied to detention fees and missed throughput targets. The system deliberately avoids identifying people, detecting only objects such as forklifts, pallets, dock doors and congestion patterns to protect worker privacy and reduce surveillance anxiety.
“Our goal all the time is to get the warehouse more capacity from the resources that they are already paying for,” Sarit Tamir, founder and CEO of Seeteria said.
“The system is completely blind to people,” Sarit Tamir, founder and CEO of Seeteria said.
Seeteria recently completed a stint at the CoLab accelerator in Chattanooga, Tennessee, after a connection made at the Home Delivery World conference in Nashville. The company announced that a new pilot launch in Chattanooga is imminent. Its name derives from the Greek goddess Soteria, but the spelling was changed from “SO” to “SEE” to reflect its computer vision focus.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/warehouse-ai-using-existing-cameras-to-cut-idle-dock-time)

item.title: DoorDash shows off under‑55‑pound delivery drone for Northern California launch
item.description:
DoorDash showed off its in‑house delivery drone on Tuesday, a six‑rotor craft weighing under 55 pounds. The drone is slated to begin deliveries in Northern California within months, carrying light orders three to five miles.
It weighs less than Amazon’s Prime Air drone, which the company lists at roughly 78 pounds. Its slow‑spinning propellers were shaped to produce a sound comparable to a passing car, aiming to reduce noise complaints. DoorDash said the first restaurant partners will be Chipotle and Popeyes. The three‑to‑five‑mile range is expected to cover about 80 % of typical DoorDash orders.
“The six-rotor drone comes in under 55 pounds, compared with the roughly 78 pounds Amazon lists for its Prime Air drone, and its slow-spinning propellers were designed so it sounds about like a passing car,” Stanley Tang, co‑founder and chief product officer said.
“The design was built around noise from the start, as Amazon’s drones face complaints from residents about their buzzing,” Harrison Shih, DoorDash Air head said.
DoorDash designed the drone in-house for its DoorDash Air service. Amazon’s Prime Air drone has drawn complaints from residents about its buzzing noise.
Source: Shopifreaks (https://shopifreaks.com/doordash-unveils-its-own-delivery-drone-which-it-says-is-lighter-and-quieter-than-amazons-ahead-of-a-northern-california-launch)

item.title: Meta launches Muse for Small Business
item.description:
Meta launched Muse for Small Business, extending its Muse personal AI agent—released in the United States and Canada earlier this month—to help owners run their businesses. Owners can link Shopify, Stripe, Intuit QuickBooks, Klaviyo, Canva, Slack, and other tools, along with Facebook Pages, Instagram professional analytics, and Meta ad accounts. From there, they can assign goals such as building a growth plan from a year of sales and campaigns, drafting next week’s ads, or flagging expenses that look wrong, with all actions pending owner approval.
Muse itself is free to use, though paid subscription plans are available for owners who need additional features. The system does not publish, send, or process payments until the owner explicitly approves each output.
Source: Shopifreaks (https://shopifreaks.com/meta-launches-muse-for-small-business-connecting-its-ai-agent-to-shopify-stripe-quickbooks-klaviyo-and-meta-ad-accounts)

item.title: Garnet Hill launches Second Nature resale site for used apparel, bedding
item.description:
Garnet Hill has launched a resale marketplace called Second Nature for its pre‑owned apparel and bedding, marking five decades in business. The marketplace lists a cashmere polo sweater for $104 (down from $189) and a lightweight twin‑sized comforter for $97 (down from $199).
Garnet Hill describes the launch as the next logical step for a brand whose products are built to last and to be passed on between friends, families, and now shoppers. The online platform was built by Archive, which powers in‑house resale solutions for brands, and each item is inspected and restored by Tersus Solutions using its proprietary waterless cleaning process. Garnet Hill plans to let consumers sell items on the site in the future, though no timeline has been set, and sellers will be able to choose cash payment or store credit. Founded in 1976 by Pegge Kirschner and Grant Dowse, the brand survived the founders’ deaths in a 1985 plane crash and was sold to QVC Group in 2017. The resale marketplace reflects an increasing consumer appetite for circularity, especially among GenZ shoppers, as seen with Depop’s $1 billion in sales last year.
“Garnet Hill Second Nature is a natural extension of that legacy giving our customers a trusted way to pass along favorite pieces and help them find a new home. By keeping quality products in circulation, they can be enjoyed for years to come and it’s better for the planet,” Connie Hallquist, president of Garnet Hill said.
“Garnet Hill has built its business on natural materials and pieces designed to last, which makes it a great fit for resale,” Emily Gittins, CEO and co-founder of Archive said.
Garnet Hill was founded in 1976 by Pegge Kirschner and Grant Dowse after they brought an English cotton flannel sheet from Europe. The founders died in a 1985 plane crash, and the business was sold to QVC Group in 2017.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/sustainability/garnet-hill-secondhand-fashion-resale-archive-1239297631)

He said brands should rethink their D2C, marketplace and social strategies to prepare for AI agents that can autonomously manage retail operations.
The Commerce layer handles transaction execution while the Intelligence layer provides decision‑making for Agentic Commerce. Rithum’s multichannel AI agents are being built to operate across direct‑to‑consumer sites, marketplaces and social platforms. The video interview notes that Agentic Commerce currently mirrors the early stages of ecommerce. Bhatt advised brands to start preparing now for a shift where AI agents will handle routine retail tasks. Bhatt noted a fundamental shift in ecommerce that is underway at present. He explained that Agentic Commerce today resembles the early days of online retail. The interview also covered practical steps for optimising retail operations within an Agentic Commerce framework. Bhatt concluded with recommendations for brands on preparing for the Agentic Commerce transition. The opening segment introduced Mausam Bhatt as Rithum’s Chief Product Officer and set the stage for the discussion. Bhatt highlighted that the current ecommerce shift is fundamental and ongoing. He described the present state of Agentic Commerce as still nascent but rapidly evolving. The talk noted that today’s Agentic Commerce resembles the early internet‑era ecommerce boom. Bhatt explained that the Commerce layer manages transactions while the Intelligence layer drives AI‑based decisions. He gave concrete advice on adjusting D2C, marketplace and social tactics for an Agentic Commerce environment. The presentation revealed that Rithum is building AI agents capable of working across multiple sales channels. item.title: AliExpress rolls out free Elite VIP program for $800-plus shoppers
item.description:
AliExpress is piloting Elite, an invitation-only VIP program for customers who spend over $800 a year, in Australia, the UK, Germany, and Spain. Unlike Amazon Prime, Elite costs nothing and gives members an extra 5% off many products, 24/7 customer service and easier returns.
AliExpress plans to roll out Elite to additional European countries and South Korea next month, with a U.S. launch date still to be decided. The company aims to enroll one million Elite members by the end of the year. Elite is part of a broader AliExpress effort that includes testing next-day delivery from local warehouses in Madrid, Paris and Warsaw. The initiative follows new tariffs and EU parcel fees that have undermined the low-cost direct-from-China shipping model. AliExpress tests Elite, a free invite-only VIP program for shoppers who spend over $800 a year, in a bid to compete with Amazon.
AliExpress had engaged in a price war with rival eCommerce firms Shein and Temu, but all three firms shifted their focus after the U.S. introduced new tariffs and the European Union placed a handling fee on packages from outside the region, the report said. As part of this shift, AliExpress is testing next-day delivery in some European cities and increasing the share of branded products in its product lineup, per the report. Alibaba Group said in an Aug. 20 press release that AliExpress achieved operating profit during the quarter ended June 30.
Source: Shopifreaks (https://shopifreaks.com/aliexpress-tests-elite-a-free-invite-only-vip-program-for-shoppers-who-spend-over-800-a-year-in-a-bid-to-compete-with-amazon)

item.title: Pinterest and Wayfair launch UK trend‑to‑shopping campaign with 4.5% sales lift
item.description:
Pinterest and Wayfair launched a UK campaign that turns top Pins into a shoppable shopping list, delivering over 4.5% incremental sales lift after analysing a 12‑month period of search data. The initiative also drove a 3.5‑point increase in action intent and a 2.5% rise in Pin awareness among UK users.
Using Pinterest UK search data, Wayfair identified two rising home‑interior themes: Cosy Spaces, focused on warm, comfortable rooms, and Dopamine Décor, which embraces bold colour and playful details. The brand turned these insights into curated product collections on Pinterest, letting users save favourite items and click through to Wayfair to purchase. The Top Pins phase ranked the ten products most saved and engaged with during the Wishlist stage, turning the most‑pinned items into a direct shopping experience.
“Pinterest gives us a really interesting view into what people are searching for and thinking about for their homes. With this campaign, we’ve been able to take those insights and turn them into something tangible, first by creating the Wayfair Wishlist around the trends people were visually searching for, and then by seeing which products people actually saved and engaged with. Top Pins brings those favourites to the forefront and shows how inspiration can translate into products people genuinely want to buy and bring into their homes,” Alberto Pontin, Head of Performance Marketing, Wayfair UK said.
“With Top Pins, Wayfair is turning the products that captured people’s imagination on Pinterest into a shoppable experience, powered by our understanding of what people are searching, saving and planning for their homes. By identifying the interior trends gaining momentum across the UK, from Cosy Spaces to Dopamine Décor, Pinterest insights have helped shape a first‑of‑its‑kind campaign that connects Wayfair with people in a way that feels relevant and useful. It also shows how Pinterest trends can help brands engage audiences with precision and authenticity,
Source: ChannelX (https://channelx.world/2026/09/pinterest-and-wayfair-turn-top-pins-into-first-of-its-kind-shopping-list)

item.title: Harbinger secures FedEx order for 2,000 electric trucks worth over $300 million
item.description:
Harbinger announced on Wednesday that FedEx has ordered 2,000 all-electric trucks in a deal valued at more than $300 million. The trucks are slated for delivery by the end of 2027 and will replace diesel vehicles one-for-one in FedEx’s U.S. and Canada pickup‑and‑delivery fleet.
Harbinger says the trucks have a 42‑foot turning diameter and include improved suspension, handling and advanced driver‑assistance technology to reduce fatigue on urban routes.
“FedEx is demonstrating that the business case for incorporating electric vehicles into real-world fleet operations at scale makes sense,” John Harris, co‑founder and CEO said.
“Electrifying a fleet at this scale requires vehicles that can perform the work our robust operations demand while also delivering meaningful economic benefits,” Paul Melander, FedEx senior vice president of safety and transportation said.
Prior to this order, FedEx had purchased 53 Harbinger electric trucks in November 2025 and co‑led the company’s $160 million Series C financing, with a FedEx executive joining Harbinger’s board.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/harbinger-fedex-2000-electric-truck-order)

item.title: Pacific rates climb high after United States-China truce extended.
item.description:
Trans-Pacific spot rates from Asia to the U.S. West Coast rose to $8,400 per forty-foot equivalent unit this week, reaching a new yearly high. East Coast spot rates held at about $9,600 per FEU, roughly $200 below their late-August peak.
The United States and China agreed last week to extend their existing trade truce by two months, postponing the Nov. 10 expiration and delaying potential U.S. port fees on China-linked vessels.
The agreement reached last week at a Washington meeting between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping extends the countries’ existing trade truce, which had been due to expire Nov. 10. The U.S. Trade Representative had not formally announced a deferral of port-call fees targeting China-linked ships as of this week.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/ocean-rates-highest-in-a-year-amid-us-china-trade-truce)

item.title: Sedex expands supply chain mapping to Tier 2 suppliers as only 12% have data
item.description:
Sedex expanded its supply chain mapping and risk assessment tools to help businesses identify individual worksites beyond direct vendors, a move announced as only 12 percent of surveyed companies have data on most Tier 2 suppliers. The update lets suppliers label their upstream connections by tier and requires approval before those links appear to downstream customers.
Sedex already offered mapping beyond direct suppliers, but the update changes how suppliers add upstream connections by letting them label those links by tier and requiring the upstream supplier's approval before the connection becomes visible to downstream customers. Once visible, corporate teams can filter suppliers and worksites by tier in Sedex's analytics dashboards to pinpoint higher-risk locations and gaps in suppliers' efforts to address problems. The expanded risk assessment tool covers 15 topics across more than 120,000 registered worksites. Its Audit Risk component draws on patterns from over 250,000 SMETA audits of 115,000 sites in 106 countries, and wage-risk calculations now use data from over 70,000 site-level SMETA audits plus external sources.
“Leaders are being asked to make increasingly important sourcing decisions in an environment that is less predictable than ever,” Jon Hancock, CEO of Sedex said.
“The hardest part of supply chain sustainability risk management is knowing where to act first,” Duncan Ellis, chief product and technology officer at Sedex said.
Sedex previously provided supply chain mapping that extended beyond direct suppliers. The latest update modifies how suppliers add upstream connections by letting them label those links by tier and requiring the upstream supplier's approval before the link is visible to downstream customers.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/logistics/sedex-supply-chain-mapping-tier-two-audit-risk-1239297790)

item.title: Sleep Country Canada brings Bed Bath & Beyond back online with 6,000 products
item.description:
Sleep Country Canada launched the Bed Bath & Beyond online store in Canada, roughly three and a half years after the Canadian chain entered creditor protection in February 2023, offering about 6,000 products from more than 80 brands. Sleep Country plans to open physical Bed Bath & Beyond stores in late 2027, marking the brand’s return to brick-and-mortar retail in Canada.
The online assortment includes roughly 6,000 items from more than 80 brands, spanning bed, bath, kitchen, dining, décor, organization, baby and seasonal goods. Sleep Country Canada secured the Canadian rights to Bed Bath & Beyond from Overstock in late 2025, after the trademarks had been pulled out of bankruptcy in 2023. All 54 former Bed Bath & Beyond locations in Canada closed when the company filed for CCAA creditor protection in February 2023. Stewart Schaefer, President & CEO of Sleep Country Canada and head of brands including Endy, Silk & Snow, Casper and Simba, said bringing Bed Bath & Beyond back to Canada is a dream come true.
“We’ve taken what people know and love about the brand and given them new reasons to discover it, with a thoughtful assortment that brings together style, function and accessibility,” Carol Deacon, President, Bed Bath & Beyond Canada said.
Bed Bath & Beyond Canada entered CCAA creditor protection in February 2023. At the time, it operated 54 stores. Sleep Country Canada acquired the brand’s rights in late 2025 after it shut down its stores.
Source: Shopifreaks (https://shopifreaks.com/bed-bath-beyond-returns-to-canada-as-an-online-store-under-sleep-country-ownership-with-physical-stores-planned-for-late-2027)

item.title: Daimler Truck aims to put driverless trucks on U.S. roads by end of 2026
item.description:
Daimler Truck’s CEO Karin Rådström said the company will have Torc-operated trucks running on public roads without a safety driver before the end of 2026. She added that the first paid freight runs are slated for 2027, with broader deployment planned for 2028.
In November 2024 Torc completed driver-out validation on a closed Texas course at speeds up to 65 mph.
“We’re building the entire autonomous trucking system, from the truck platform and vehicle architecture to the hardware integration and also the autonomous driving software,” Karin Rådström, CEO of Daimler Truck said.
“For the first time, a Torc truck will be able to drive itself on public roads — not on a test track — and without a safety driver in the cab,” Karin Rådström, CEO of Daimler Truck said.
Torc previously demonstrated driver‑out operation on a closed Texas track in November 2024 at up to 65 mph. Freightliner and Western Star together held 37.8% of the North American Class 8 market through June, according to Daimler’s investor presentation.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/daimler-truck-torc-autonomous-system)

item.title: Port Houston lifts August container volumes 1% as steel imports jump 54%
item.description:
Port Houston’s public terminals handled 373,756 twenty-foot equivalent units in August, a 1% increase from the same month last year. Steel imports reached 502,965 tons in August, up 54% from a year earlier.
Loaded imports totaled 176,016 TEUs in August, a 4% rise from a year earlier, while loaded exports fell 2% to 136,070 TEUs, with machinery, electronics, retail consumer goods, furniture, automotive products, and apparel cited as import commodities and seasonal front‑loading noted as a contributing factor. Through August 2026, Port Houston’s container volumes totaled 2.97 million TEUs, up 1% year over year, with loaded imports up 5% to 1.39 million TEUs, loaded exports down 1% to 1.06 million TEUs, and overall loaded container activity up 2% to 2.45 million TEUs. Vessel activity on the Houston Ship Channel increased in August, with deep‑draft transits rising 9% to 1,607 and barge transits up 10% to 19,712, both measures up 7% year to date. Port Houston approved design work for a refrigerated container yard at Bayport Container Yard 9 to hold over 1,800 units, completed 10 FTZ site authorizations matching its 2024 record with 11 under review, and welcomed the first vessel of Crowley Maritime’s Houston‑Central America service.
Although August steel imports jumped 54% year over year, year‑to‑date steel tonnage through August was down 10% to about 2.87 million tons, with imports down 11% to roughly 2.71 million tons. General cargo fell 26% in August to 116,881 tons but remained up 22% year to date at 913,863 tons, including a 27% rise in imports.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/port-houston-container-volumes-edge-higher-as-steel-imports-surge-54)

item.title: Panama Canal Adds Transit Slot, Raises Draft to 49 Feet as Water Improves
item.description:
The Panama Canal Authority increased the daily Neopanamax transit slots from nine to 10 starting Oct. 15 and raised the maximum authorized draft to 49 feet. The change lifts total daily capacity across the Neopanamax and Panamax locks to 33 slots and replaces the previous 48‑foot draft limit that took effect Tuesday.
The draft increase follows a postponement of a planned Oct. 1 reduction to 47.5 feet after the authority reassessed weather forecasts and water levels at Gatún Lake. As of Wednesday, the canal projected Gatún Lake’s average level for October at 85.7 feet, up from the earlier forecast of 82.6 feet under a severe El Niño scenario. The authority cited current and projected lake levels, near-average precipitation across the watershed and the water‑saving measures in place at the locks as reasons for the reversal. Officials warned that the water deficit persists, that the transit reservation system remains the only way to guarantee a date, and that vessels without reservations could face indefinite delays. The advisory to shipping companies on Monday specified that the additional Neopanamax slot is available for bookings starting Oct. 15.
Earlier in September the canal had cut daily transits from 36 to 34 on Sept. 4 and then again to 32 on Sept. 15 as El Niño threatened water supplies. A fiscal 2027 budget draft submitted to Panama’s parliament had penciled in an average of 29.5 daily transits for October, based on a severe El Niño outlook. In late August, the canal’s own outlook had Gatún Lake’s water levels falling by more than a foot by the end of October to 82.6 feet.
Source: WWD (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/logistics/panama-canal-eases-draft-restrictions-el-nino-water-levels-weather-trade-1239297242)

item.title: Cargo thieves launder freight in as little as one week, Cornell warns
item.description:
Cargo thieves can steal a load, change its paperwork and return it to legitimate trade within about one week. In a case involving a popular headphone brand, stolen devices were detected in Europe roughly seven days after the theft.
Thieves move the stolen pallets through a cross‑dock, warehouse or even a parking lot, where they swap the original bill of lading for a new one. They may re‑label the cargo as generic electronics or as freight of all kinds (FAK) and attach a fresh bolt seal. Because paper documents still carry more authority than electronic tracking, the altered paperwork makes the goods appear legitimate during later moves. Cornell said digital bills of lading could close that gap, but getting the whole supply chain onto compatible systems remains the bigger hurdle. He suggested a phased requirement could eventually bring companies onto the same digital standard, similar to the shift to electronic logging devices in trucking.
“Bill of lading and bolt seal trump it all,” Scott Cornell, EVP, Crime and Theft Specialist at SPG Cargo & Logistics and chair of TAPA Americas said.
“They’re hiding in plain sight in a lot of these cases,” Scott Cornell, EVP, Crime and Theft Specialist at SPG Cargo & Logistics and chair of TAPA Americas said.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/cargo-thieves-are-laundering-freight-through-the-supply-chain-cornell-warns)

item.title: Wix launches Base Code for non-engineers to edit GitHub code via prompts
item.description:
Wix’s Base44 launched Base Code to all its users as a separate product that connects GitHub repos to cloud workspaces where teams edit an existing codebase through plain-language requests. Wix acquired Base44 for $80 million in 2025, and now offers Base Code as a standalone product.
Product managers, designers, QA, and operations staff can type changes into chat, see a live preview, and submit them as pull requests that engineers still review. Workspace owners can limit which GitHub organizations a project may be imported from, and all secrets are stored encrypted. While Base44’s original app builder creates new apps from prompts, Base Code modifies existing production software.
Source: Shopifreaks (https://shopifreaks.com/wixs-base44-launches-base-code-which-connects-github-repos-to-cloud-workspaces-where-non-engineers-can-change-code-by-prompt)

item.title: Fast fashion brands post 364k tons output in 2025 despite sustainability claims
item.description:
Fast fashion brands reported higher output in 2025 while promoting sustainability initiatives, with H&M producing 364,093 metric tons of products. Inditex’s raw material use rose to 705,554 metric tons in 2025, up from 678,596 tons the prior year.
Shein’s platform listed as many as 600,000 items for sale at any time, underscoring the scale of its fast‑fashion model. In 2025, H&M, Zara and Shein generated roughly $23.5 billion, $46.3 billion and over $50 billion in sales respectively. Despite claims that 91% of H&M’s materials and 88% of Inditex’s fibers are lower‑impact, the companies together produced over a million metric tons of apparel, contributing to significant waste streams.
“Our starting point is always our business idea: fashion and quality at the best price in a sustainable way,” Daniel Ervér, CEO of H&M said.
“The fast fashion business model, by design, is difficult, if not altogether impossible, to be made sustainable,” Javad Nasiry, professor of operations management at McGill University said.
In 2016 H&M pledged to become a circular company by 2040 through a partnership with the Ellen MacArthur Foundation. The goal involves creating products designed to last from safe, recycled or sustainably sourced materials that can recirculate multiple times.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/sustainable-fast-fashion-paradox-or-possibility/831641)

item.title: USPS and Amazon start same-day delivery pilot for 200 packages
item.description:
USPS and Amazon launched a same-day delivery pilot on Tuesday at the Morgantown, West Virginia, and Lake Havasu City, Arizona, facilities, limiting each site to 200 packages. Under the pilot, Amazon parcels dropped off between 12 p.m. and 1 p.m. local time are sorted and delivered by city mail carriers between 2 p.m. and 8 p.m. the same day. Each location will operate three designated delivery routes, with no set end date for the trial.
The pilot is scheduled to expand to the USPS sorting and delivery center in Columbia, South Carolina, on October 20, where the volume cap will rise to 500 packages and five required routes. Amazon said it has spent more than $5 billion with the Postal Service in recent years, making the partnership a notable revenue source for the agency. The initiative builds on a January USPS bidding process that lets shippers reserve last‑mile capacity for same‑day or next‑day delivery. Amazon also noted that orders placed later in the day would now qualify for same‑day delivery through the pilot, while the overall process remains unchanged.
“For example, orders placed later in the day would now be eligible for same day delivery through this pilot, the process is the same otherwise,” Terrence Clark, Amazon spokesperson said.
Amazon has rapidly expanded its in‑house delivery network but still relies on the Postal Service for a share of its shipments. Earlier this year the two companies reached a scaled‑back shipping agreement, and in January the USPS launched a bidding process for shippers to reserve last‑mile capacity for same‑day or next‑day delivery.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/usps-amazon-partner-on-same-day-delivery-pilot/831647)

item.title: Circle CFO Jeremy Fox-Geen Departs in December After Five Years
item.description:
Circle CFO Jeremy Fox-Geen will depart the company in December after five years in the role. His departure comes shortly after Circle’s June 2025 IPO raised $1.05 billion at an $8 billion valuation.
Fox-Geen will remain CFO through Dec. 31 or until a successor is named, continuing to earn his $500,000 base salary and eligibility for a 2026 target bonus of 110% of that pay. Upon leaving, he will receive a $1.05 million severance paid in monthly installments over a year and accelerated vesting of restricted stock units equal to two additional months. Circle also announced a new $100 million equity investment from Binance under a five‑year agreement to expand USDC into emerging markets. Co‑founder P. Sean Neville stepped down from the board immediately, reducing its size from eight to seven members.
“key role in building Circle to the company it is today,” Jeremy Allaire, CEO and Chairman said.
“Serving as Circle's Chief Financial Officer has been the highlight of my professional career,” Jeremy Fox-Geen, CFO said.
Fox-Geen, a former McKinsey & Company and PricewaterhouseCoopers analyst, joined Circle in 2021 and helped guide the firm through its June 2025 IPO after several earlier abandoned attempts to go public.
Source: Payments Dive (https://paymentsdive.com/news/circle-cfo-step-down-following-ipo-leadership-crypto-comp/831712)

item.title: DoorDash launches Dasher Returns and adds five new retailers to its marketplace
item.description:
On Sept. 29, DoorDash launched its Dasher Returns service in select cities and announced a nationwide rollout for November. The company expects Dasher Returns to be available for 80% of the retail orders it handles by the end of 2026.
For a flat fee, DoorDash will pick up a customer’s return at home and deliver it to the merchant’s store for processing. Once the item is back in stock, the store can resell it quickly and issue the refund in days rather than weeks. DoorDash also added Anthropologie, North Face, Timberland, Vans and Macy’s to its marketplace app, making their products searchable for same‑day delivery. Macy’s said its full catalog will be available inside the DoorDash Marketplace app and that DoorDash will join its 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City on Nov. 26.
“Starting today, we’re launching Dasher Returns,” Shanna Prevé, chief revenue officer at DoorDash said.
“Now, today we are announcing that the Macy’s catalog will be available from within the DoorDash Marketplace app,” Josh Janos, vice president of marketplaces and digital partnerships at Macy’s said.
Earlier this year, DoorDash began delivering Costco orders in the U.S. and tested drone delivery with Lowe’s and Wing. Macy’s had been using DoorDash for white‑label same‑day and next‑day fulfillment since 2020 for orders placed through its website and apps.
Source: Digital Commerce 360 (https://digitalcommerce360.com/2026/09/30/doordash-prepares-nationwide-returns-service-welcomes-new-retailers-to-marketplace)

item.title: Hormuz closure risks permanent transhipment loss at Jebel Ali and Khalifa
item.description:
The Hormuz Strait closure, now approaching its eighth month, is predicted to cause a permanent loss of transhipment traffic at the UAE’s Jebel Ali and Khalifa ports. DP World is constructing 2.5 million TEU of capacity outside the Hormuz Strait to offset expected losses. Gulftainer plans to raise Khor Fakkan’s annual capacity from 3.5 million to 10 million TEU, positioning the port as a Gulf bypass.
Insurance premiums for vessels transiting the Hormuz Strait have risen from pre‑war levels of 0.1‑0.2% of hull value to between 2.5% and 7.5%. In July, DP World secured a 50‑year concession with Fujairah Port Authority to build two terminals outside the strait. Carriers such as MSC, CMA CGM and Maersk have already shifted calls to alternatives like Khor Fakkan, Sohar, Salalah, Colombo, Vizhinjam and Jeddah.
“Relay transhipment doesn’t come back – ever,” Eirik Hooper, Drewry’s senior associate for ports and terminals said.
“Insurers will not restore pre-2026 pricing for a strait that’s been mined and blockaded, and a hub whose access carries a persistent risk premium and cannot win price-sensitive relay cargo against a Salalah or Colombo – that’s structural, not cyclical,” Eirik Hooper, Drewry’s senior associate for ports and terminals said.
Prior to the outbreak of the US-Israel-Iran conflict, the two UAE ports were a favoured waypoint for relay transhipment operations – boxes moving between Asia-Europe vessels and ships deployed on north-south trades. Both DP World and AD Ports reported huge declines in first half volumes at Jebel Ali and Khalifa respectively, due the war, forcing their owners to look elsewhere for growth.
Source: The Loadstar (https://theloadstar.com/hormuz-closure-a-fatal-blow-for-dubai-and-abu-dhabi-transhipment-volumes)

item.title: Cook County sheriff’s cargo theft blitz recovers $635,000 in stolen freight
item.description:
Cook County Sheriff’s Police led a 24‑hour National Supply Chain Blitz on Sept. 23‑24, resulting in the recovery of about $635,000 in stolen cargo. The effort, described as the nation’s first coordinated operation focused specifically on cargo theft, recovered thirty transformers worth roughly $600,000 of the total.
Federal, state and local law enforcement agencies worked with railroad police from Norfolk Southern, Union Pacific, BNSF Railway and CSX, as well as private security groups such as CargoNet, TAPA, Overhaul, LPRC, Class8 and 3SI Security Systems.
“Criminal networks don’t respect jurisdictional lines,” Commander Michael Ware, incident commander said.
Officials described the effort as the nation’s first coordinated operation focused specifically on cargo theft.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/national-cargo-theft-blitz-leads-to-arrests-635k-in-recovered-freight)

item.title: Podcast examines where freight forwarders lose margin and how to stop it
item.description:
The Loadstar Podcast released an episode examining where freight forwarders lose money between booking and delivery and how they can protect their margins. The discussion centers on where money leaks occur between booking and delivery and what forwarders can do to protect margins.
Detention and demurrage fees, rate mismatches, and unbilled expenses can eat into a forwarder’s profit. Manual processing and rework add further costs, while Metro tests new technology in pilots before wider rollout. Both guests argue that reliable data, clear processes, and human oversight matter more than simply adding another AI tool.
“In this episode of The Loadstar Podcast, host Charlotte Goldstone asks where freight forwarders lose money between booking and delivery, and what they can do to protect their margins,” Charlotte Goldstone, host of The Loadstar Podcast said.
“Emma Crumpton, enterprise solutions director at Portcast, explains how detention and demurrage charges, mismatched buy and sell rates, and costs that are never billed back to customers can erode the return on a job,” Emma Crumpton, enterprise solutions director at Portcast said.
Source: The Loadstar (https://theloadstar.com/where-forwarders-lose-margin-and-how-to-stop-it)

item.title: Subscription spending grows 7.7% YoY in July 2026, outpacing overall card spend
item.description:
Bank of America’s analysis showed non-utility subscription spending rose 7.7% year on year in July 2026, outpacing overall card spending growth. Entertainment subscriptions alone now account for about 43% of all subscription spending, according to the research.
Spending on information and AI-related subscriptions grew 61% year on year among Gen Z consumers and 51% among younger millennials. Overall, Gen Z posted the fastest subscription spending growth at nearly 14% year on year in July 2026, while Gen X remained the largest spending cohort. The bank noted that the upward trend in subscription spending has persisted for two years, indicating continued consumer willingness to commit to recurring payments despite economic uncertainty.
Bank of America’s research notes that subscription spending has been growing faster than overall consumer spending, driven by entertainment, retail memberships and information services. The bank’s latest analysis found this trend has persisted for two years.
Source: InternetRetailing (https://internetretailing.net/subscription-spending-continues-to-outpace-wider-consumer-spending-growth)

item.title: Cakes Body launches internal entertainment arm after $100M sales
item.description:
Cakes Body launched its internal entertainment company, Cakes Media, last week to turn its TikTok virality into an owned media strategy. The brand, which launched in 2022, has grossed $100 million in sales over three years.
The company hired former Red Bull executive Caley Wildermuth to lead content for Cakes Media. Its first release is a 57‑minute documentary on YouTube that has attracted more than 371,600 views. Cakes Media is funded from the brand’s top‑of‑funnel marketing budget, and the firm plans to cut full‑length episodes into short‑form clips for platforms like TikTok and Instagram. The founders describe the effort as a test‑and‑learn phase to determine which content formats resonate most with audiences while building long‑term engagement.
“To have that humanness and personality come through, it’s hard to outsource that [organic social content] to an agency,” Taylor Capuano said.
“Entertainment has become the new price of admission. Brands must earn attention by offering entertaining content,” Daryl Giannantonio said.
Cakes Body founders Taylor Capuano and Casey Sarai built the brand primarily through founder‑led storytelling and TikTok viral videos, avoiding traditional brand marketing spend. The company appeared on Shark Tank and has cited brands like Bogg Bag and Stanley as comparable in their reliance on creator‑driven content. The move follows a trend seen with brands such as Red Bull Media House, which create in‑house studios to produce television shows, films or microseries.
Source: Glossy (https://glossy.co/beauty/beauty-brand-cakes-wants-to-turn-its-tiktok-virality-into-an-owned-media-strategy)

item.title: Oil prices fall as Gulf crude flows near pre-war levels, diesel down 14.7 cents
item.description:
Oil prices fell Tuesday as reports showed crude flows from the Persian Gulf nearing pre-war levels, pushing the weekly retail diesel price down 14.7 cents to $6.382 per gallon. It marked the first weekly diesel price decline in four weeks, ending a three-week streak of record highs.
JP Morgan reported that product exports from the Gulf remain only slightly above 50% of pre-war levels, while crude flows are closer to normal. ULSD futures on the CME settled at $4.6847/g on Friday after falling from a September 16 high of $5.262/g, then rebounded Monday and Tuesday as the October contract neared expiration. Texas Governor Greg Abbott issued a disaster proclamation allowing dyed diesel for on-road use and requested a temporary EPA waiver on ultra-low sulfur diesel rules.
Prior to this week, diesel prices had risen for three consecutive weeks, reaching new all-time highs each week. The September 16 ULSD futures settlement had marked a recent peak of $5.262 per gallon. Oil markets had been pressured by concerns over Iran’s ability to restrict flows through the Strait of Hormuz.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/more-oil-out-of-the-gulf-translating-to-lower-prices)

item.title: Shein reports 298 million Q2 orders as profit slips two‑thirds
item.description:
Shein fulfilled 298 million orders between April and June, 21 million more than a year earlier, while first‑half adjusted net income fell 55.6% to $499 million. Revenue for the half edged up 1% to $20.13 billion, but the company’s market value slid to about $16.8 billion after shares fell as much as 12.1% to a record low.
Fulfilment expenses rose 18.1% to $5.59 billion, absorbing 50.4% of revenue versus 43.1% a year earlier. Fulfilment and marketing together consumed about 64 cents of each revenue dollar, up from 57 cents previously. US revenue fell 6% to $2.47 billion in the quarter, Europe revenue dropped 13.9% to $3.77 billion, and rest‑of‑world sales rose 21.6% to $4.84 billion.
“The compression was primarily driven by a sharp spike in oil prices and freight rates amid Middle East geopolitical tensions,” Sky Xu, Shein’s founder, chairman and chief executive said.
“We made a deliberate decision to absorb these costs – which we view as transitory – rather than pass them through to consumers, maintaining a consistent pricing experience and order momentum,” Sky Xu, Shein’s founder, chairman and chief executive said.
In the first quarter, US revenue dropped 14.3% and the company described a continued recovery of its US business; across the half, US revenue was down about 10%. Ahead of the EU’s removal of the customs duty exemption on July 1, Shein raised prices and cut online advertising in Europe, where revenue fell 13.9% to $3.77 billion and average monthly users fell to 128 million by June.
Source: Inside Retail Asia (https://insideretail.asia/2026/09/30/inside-sheins-first-report-card-298-million-orders-a-two-thirds-profit-slump)

item.title: eBay opens Promoted Stores ads to sellers, allows 1,000 listings per campaign
item.description:
On September 29, eBay opened Custom Promoted Stores ads to all eligible sellers, letting them choose up to 1,000 listings for each campaign. The update also lets sellers direct buyers to custom landing pages such as influencer-led pages and eBay Live events.
Sellers can create a Custom Promoted Stores campaign via the Advertising tab in Seller Hub and select up to ten featured listings to highlight in their ads. The custom landing page URL must start with https:// and point to an eBay page, working with Store pages, sale event pages, eBay Live events, and influencer pages. Campaigns can be built around seasonal inventory, new arrivals, priority products, promotions, or other key moments.
Promoted Stores Custom was first announced in January, when eBay said the new option would allow sellers to select up to 1,000 listings, including ten featured items, and choose custom landing pages such as sales events, curated collections, influencer-led pages and eBay Live events. Previously, much of the campaign creation for Promoted Stores was automatically handled by eBay, leaving sellers limited to Store category pages or active coupons and unable to pick specific items to feature. Although the January announcement suggested immediate availability, eBay later confirmed access was limited while it continued testing.
Source: Value Added Resource (https://valueaddedresource.net/ebay-expands-custom-promoted-stores-ads)

item.title: Two-thirds of BNPL users abandon cart lacking preferred provider
item.description:
Two-thirds of paycheck-to-paycheck BNPL users would likely abandon a cart missing their preferred provider, according to a Morning Consult survey commissioned by Sezzle. Over a third of that group had been turned down by a BNPL service before, while 82% said BNPL let them buy something they’d otherwise have put off or skipped. Gen Z users rely on BNPL far more than Boomers, with 72% using it twice a month or more compared to 27% of Boomers.
85% of Gen Z users have tried more than one provider. Sezzle says it approves over 90% of applicants based on its own data. Sezzle is pitching the survey findings to retailers as a reason to add a second BNPL option before Black Friday.
Source: Shopifreaks (https://shopifreaks.com/two-thirds-of-paycheck-to-paycheck-bnpl-users-would-likely-abandon-a-cart-missing-their-preferred-provider-per-sezzle-survey)

item.title: Flexport launches MCP server letting AI agents book freight
item.description:
On Tuesday, Flexport launched a Model Context Protocol server that lets shippers’ AI agents track, quote, and book freight on its platform. The company said more than 13,000 companies use its platform. Flexport’s own AI agents process 21 million tasks a year.
Agents can track shipments, surface exceptions or customs holds, search rates on any lane, or book outright without logging into the Flexport platform. The server also extends Flexport Atlas beyond ocean freight, adding air, rail, and barge routing and an AI‑curated disruption layer that monitors news for shipment‑affecting events. Flexport opened its first fully automated e‑commerce fulfillment center outside Chicago, where more than 350 robots bring inventory to workers and the site runs at double the efficiency of a traditional warehouse.
“The future of global logistics is autonomous: intelligent supply chains that see problems before they happen, calculate the fix, and execute it in a recurring self‑improvement loop,” Ryan Petersen, founder and CEO of Flexport said.
In February, Flexport introduced Atlas as a no‑cost map of global trade showing the ocean network. Since then, the company has opened fulfillment centers in Mississauga, Ontario, and Manchester, England, and expanded to eight new countries, bringing its total to 47 offices worldwide.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/flexport-mcp-server-ai-agents-freight-booking)

item.title: Covenant CEO says market healthier as load-to-truck ratios ease to 1.3‑to‑1.5
item.description:
Covenant Logistics Group founder and CEO David Parker said load-to-truck ratios cooled from roughly two-to-one in the first half of 2025 to 1.3-to-1.5 starting in July and August, calling the shift healthier and more sustainable heading into peak season. He noted that in the second quarter, most truckload carriers posted double-digit rate increases, yet operating ratios improved only about one point because costs rose just as fast. Covenant’s 2023 acquisition of Lou Thompson, a live-haul chicken carrier, has expanded from about 230 trucks to 800 trucks.
Covenant’s fleet is now approximately 60% Freightliner and 40% Peterbilt, with roughly 100 solo over-the-road trucks remaining as the company exits commoditized OTR freight.
“We need another double-digit rate if this industry’s gonna stay healthy,” David Parker, CEO of Covenant Logistics Group said.
“I have not found one customer willing to pay for that electric truck yet — not one, unless it’s California,” David Parker, CEO of Covenant Logistics Group said.
David Parker, CEO of Covenant Logistics Group, discusses the evolving freight landscape, including the impact of emissions standards, the move away from commoditized OTR, and surprising insights into specialized markets like live chicken hauling. He shares his views on the future of electric and autonomous trucks, and how economic factors like GLP-1 drugs are affecting consumer freight.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/the-freight-market-is-healthier-than-you-think)

item.title: Gartner says only 5% will automate 10% of supply chain planning by 2030
item.description:
Gartner predicts that only 5 percent of organizations implementing supply chain automation will automate at least 10 percent of their planning decisions by 2030. The forecast, based on Gartner surveys and client interactions, distinguishes between AI that supports decisions and AI that makes them autonomous.
Gartner’s survey polled 394 supply chain professionals from companies with at least $250 million in annual revenue. Despite $40 billion in enterprise AI investment, a MIT study found 95 percent of organizations are not yet seeing any returns. A Kinaxis poll of over 2,000 leaders showed 41 percent expect autonomous supply chains at scale within one to two years, while only one in eight have fully embedded AI governance.
“Spending millions on supply chain planning automation can expand technical capabilities, but investment alone does not create AI readiness,” Buse Aras, director analyst in Gartner’s supply chain practice said.
In August, a Gartner survey showed that more than half of supply chain officers were unsure about their AI return on investment despite significant spending. A MIT landmark study found that despite funneling $40 billion into enterprise investment, 95 percent of organizations are not yet seeing any returns. Earlier this year, Kinaxis surveyed over 2,000 supply chain leaders across nine markets, reporting that two‑fifths (41 percent) expect autonomous supply chains at scale within one to two years, while only one in eight have been fully embedded with AI governance.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/gartner-report-prediction-ai-1239285682)

item.title: Kodiak to launch driverless IKEA freight on Texas I-45 later this year
item.description:
Kodiak AI will haul IKEA freight with no one in the cab on a 219-mile stretch of Interstate 45 in Texas later this year. IKEA Supply is the launch shipper for the service, which forms part of an existing 292-mile route between its Baytown distribution center and Frisco store.
The driverless trips mainly operate between Kodiak’s facilities in Houston and the Dallas area. In the last four years, Kodiak moved over 1,300 IKEA loads autonomously with a safety observer, covering more than 750,000 miles. Starting in August, Kodiak launched its driverless long-haul program and now regularly hauls freight between its Lancaster, Texas hub and Houston without anyone behind the wheel. Kodiak’s autonomy readiness measure was 93% at the end of August, up from 84% in February, and the company expects to reach 100% and launch driverless operations by year-end.
“Unsupervised driverless operations – no human in the cab – represent a milestone the entire Kodiak team has been tirelessly working toward since Kodiak was founded more than eight years ago,” Don Burnette, founder and CEO, Kodiak AI said.
“They can reduce their time sleeping on the side of the highway and instead be home with family and friends,” Don Burnette, founder and CEO, Kodiak AI said.
Over the past four years, Kodiak has delivered more than 1,300 loads and logged more than 750,000 miles carrying IKEA goods autonomously with a safety observer aboard, founder and CEO Don Burnette wrote in a company post announcing the partnership update. The company began its driverless long-haul launch program in August and said it now consistently completes deliveries between its Lancaster, Texas, hub and Houston without human intervention. Kodiak already runs driverless trucks commercially for Atlas Energy Solutions in the Permian Basin, work that began in December 2024.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/kodiak-ikea-driverless-freight-i-45)

item.title: Happy Returns integrates with TikTok Shop to offer box‑free returns
item.description:
Happy Returns announced on Tuesday that its reverse‑logistics platform is now integrated into TikTok Shop, providing shoppers a box‑free, label‑free return option. The integration targets a market where TikTok Shop logged over 103 billion searches in the U.S. in 2025 and where mail‑in returns are six times more prone to fraud than in‑person drops.
Shoppers can start a return in the TikTok app and drop off items at any of Happy Returns’ Return Bar locations nationwide, receiving an instant refund without needing a box or a label. The option is available to participating retailers whether they fulfill orders themselves or rely on TikTok Shop’s fulfillment service. Happy Returns already processes returns for brands such as Everlane, Allbirds, Shein, Fabletics, Revolve and Under Armour.
“Our TikTok Shop partnership brings Happy Returns into one of the fastest-growing commerce ecosystems, giving greater confidence at purchase while supporting the fraud-resistant, scalable returns infrastructure merchants need to grow,” David Sobie, co‑founder and CEO of Happy Returns said.
“Our collaboration with Happy Returns builds on our commitment to making the returns experience faster, hassle‑free, and more trustworthy for our shoppers, with box‑free, label‑free returns and instant refunds at approximately 10,000 Return Bar locations nationwide,” Patrick Nommensen, president of strategic initiatives at TikTok Shop said.
Happy Returns already handles returns for brands including Everlane, Allbirds, Shein, Fabletics, Revolve and Under Armour.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/happy-returns-is-now-intergrates-into-tiktok-1239287966)

item.title: Airbus completes first test flight of A350 freighter, targets late-2027 delivery
item.description:
Airbus completed the first test flight of its A350 widebody freighter on Tuesday, reaching 25,000 feet and flying for four hours and ten minutes. The manufacturer has tallied 103 orders from 14 customers and expects the first commercial delivery in late 2027.
The freighter offers a payload of 111 metric tons and features the industry's widest cargo door at 175 inches.
“We can say it has been built by Airbus, but really it has been designed by the market. The market was sending us a very strong signal. Operators were coming to us to say they wanted choice. They didn’t want just one option in terms of what they could buy for a large freighter,” Sarah McLaren, head of widebody and freighter marketing said.
Airbus began designing the A350 freighter last decade, basing it on the successful A350-1000 passenger aircraft. The freighter is intended to be Airbus’s first production aircraft capable of challenging Boeing’s dominance in the cargo market.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/airbus-a350-freighter-aircraft-completes-initial-test-flight)

item.title: Senate passes Common Cents bill to phase out penny
item.description:
The Senate passed the Common Cents bill on Monday night, sending the legislation to the White House for President Donald Trump’s signature. The legislation provides merchants with a legal framework to round cash transactions to the nearest nickel and formally ends U.S. Mint production of the penny.
The measure does not apply to electronic transactions, covering only cash purchases. Retailers, especially grocers, have faced difficulties obtaining pennies, which complicates SNAP transactions because equal‑treatment rules bar different prices for food‑assistance shoppers. After an August Senate amendment triggered a second House vote earlier this month, the bill cleared the Senate again on Monday following its earlier August passage. The bill was sponsored by Senators Cynthia Lummis (R‑WY) and Kirsten Gillibrand (D‑NY), with House cosponsors Lisa McClain (R‑MI) and Robert Garcia (D‑CA).
“a solution to a real problem for retailers,” Dylan Jeon, vice president of government relations for the National Retail Federation said.
“Independent grocers process millions of transactions every day, and the disappearance of the penny created a very practical problem at the checkout counter,” Stephanie Johnson, senior vice president and head of government affairs for the National Grocers Association said.
The bill had previously cleared the House and Senate in August after a Senate amendment, necessitating a second House vote earlier this month and a final Senate ratification on Monday. The final batch of pennies was struck last November, nine months after President Trump directed the U.S. Treasury to halt penny production.
Source: Payments Dive (https://paymentsdive.com/news/senate-passes-common-cents-bill/831629)

item.title: Democrats propose tying AGOA duty‑free access to environmental enforcement
item.description:
Democratic lawmakers introduced legislation this week that would make duty‑free access under the African Growth and Opportunity Act for 32 sub‑Saharan African countries contingent on enforcing their own environmental laws. The bill comes as AGOA’s current authorization runs through December 31, 2028 after a two‑year extension signed by President Trump on September 2.
ECO AGOA would add mandatory environmental compliance to the eligibility criteria without creating new standards, requiring beneficiary nations to enforce existing laws and meet international commitments. It would apply to the more than 1,800 products currently covered, including apparel, textiles, and footwear, across the 32 participating African nations. Examples cited by lawmakers include Lesotho textile mills accused of releasing untreated wastewater, Kenyan apparel manufacturers fined for poor effluent treatment, and Madagascar factories alleged to skirt water‑treatment rules.
“Without environmental accountability criteria, the fossil fuel industry and other big polluters rake in more profits while harming the health of local communities and putting U.S. manufacturers that use clean production methods at a disadvantage,” Senator Sheldon Whitehouse, Democrat of Rhode Island said.
“ECO AGOA sets a simple standard: If you want America’s trade preferences, enforce your own environmental laws. It is a modest step that helps our partners protect their own people and resources,” Representative Lloyd Doggett, Democrat of Texas said.
AGOA’s authorization was set to expire at the end of 2026 after Congress restored the program retroactively in February following a lapse that began in September 2025. President Trump signed a two‑year extension on September 2, extending the program through December 31, 2028.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/sustainability/eco-agoa-environmental-requirements-legslation-1239285488)

item.title: Pacsun summit shows Gen Z trusts friends over AI and influencers
item.description:
Pacsun’s second-annual Purpose Summit, held last week, revealed that Generation Z relies more on friends and family than on influencers or artificial intelligence, based on its 2026 Youth Report. While 85 percent of young people use AI, just 2 percent trust it for fashion advice and 5 percent for financial advice.
The summit, hosted at Soho House’s Little Beach House Malibu, featured speakers from Snapchat, Rare Beauty, the Los Angeles Rams and Angel City FC, among others. It also marked the first public appearance of the second cohort of Pacsun’s Youth Council, which gives younger consumers a voice through strategy sessions, workshops and executive mentorship. Discussions centered on the report’s finding that Gen Z is pulling closer to family and friends while becoming more selective about noisy online environments shaped by algorithms and inauthentic messaging. The event opened with a guided meditation led by Tai Beauchamp, founder of Tai Media, instead of a traditional keynote.
“The Purpose Summit gives us an opportunity to take what we’re hearing from young people and put it into conversation with the people helping shape the world around them,” Brieane Olson, CEO of Pacsun said.
“The data showed that young people are becoming more intentional about the relationships, influences and priorities closest to them,” Neil Saunders, managing director and retail analyst at GlobalData said.
Pacsun held its first Purpose Summit the previous year, establishing an annual forum for youth insights. The retailer’s Youth Council launched earlier, with its first cohort already advising the brand. The 2026 Youth Report was developed in partnership with GlobalData to inform the summit’s discussions.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/pacsun-summit-reveals-gen-z-pulls-up-the-drawbridge-on-ai-1239283808)
